questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG):
1. The CAG is appointed by the President and can be removed on the same grounds and in the same manner as a judge of the Supreme Court.
2. After ceasing to hold office, the CAG is eligible for further office under the Government of India or a State.
3. The salary of the CAG and the administrative expenses of the office are charged to the Consolidated Fund of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Art 148 gives the Supreme Court judge-like removal, and the salary and office expenses are charged on the Consolidated Fund, so Parliament cannot vote on them. Statement 2 is wrong: Art 148(4) bars the CAG from any further office under the Union or a State, to keep him free of any wish to please the executive.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Comptroller and Auditor General of India

questions.q: Which one of the following correctly describes the role of the CAG in relation to the Public Accounts Committee (PAC)?
o: The CAG acts as the friend, philosopher and guide of the PAC, and his reports form the basis of its work
The CAG is an ex officio member of the PAC and votes on its reports
The CAG is appointed by the PAC and reports to it alone
The PAC audits the accounts and the CAG only scrutinises its findings
questions.e: The CAG submits audit reports to the President or Governor, who has them laid before the legislature; the PAC then examines them with the CAG's assistance. The CAG is not a member of the PAC and is not appointed by it.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Comptroller and Auditor General of India; Parliamentary Committees

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Finance Commission:
1. It is a constitutional body under Article 280 that is constituted by the President every fifth year or earlier.
2. Its recommendations are binding on the Union Government.
3. It recommends the distribution of net proceeds of taxes between the Union and the States.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Art 280 requires the President to constitute the Commission every fifth year or earlier, and it recommends the sharing of net tax proceeds. Its recommendations are only advisory; the Union lays them before Parliament with an explanatory memorandum on action taken.

questions.q:
With reference to the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC), consider the following statements:
1. The Chairman and members are appointed by the President.
2. They hold office for six years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
3. The Chairman can be removed by the President for misbehaviour only after the Supreme Court, on a reference, reports that he should be removed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Arts 316 and 317 give appointment by the President, a term of six years or age 65, and removal for misbehaviour only after a Supreme Court inquiry. During the inquiry the President may suspend the member concerned.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a function of the Union Public Service Commission under the Constitution?
o: Advising the President on the transfer and posting of civil servants within the Union
Conducting examinations for appointments to the services of the Union
Advising on the principles to be followed in making civil service appointments
Advising on disciplinary matters affecting a person serving under the Government of India
questions.e: Art 320 gives UPSC examination, recruitment-method and disciplinary-consultation functions. It has no role in postings or transfers, which remain executive matters.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC):
1. It was established by the 89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003, by splitting the earlier joint Commission for SCs and STs.
2. It is provided for under Article 338 of the Constitution.
3. It has the powers of a civil court while investigating complaints.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 89th Amendment (2003) replaced the single Art 338 body with the NCSC (Art 338) and the NCST (Art 338A). While inquiring into complaints the Commission has all the powers of a civil court trying a suit.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Body)
A. National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
B. National Commission for Backward Classes
C. Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
D. Inter-State Council
List-II (Article)
1. Article 338B
2. Article 338A
3. Article 350B
4. Article 263
Which one of the following is the correct matching?
questions.e: NCST is Art 338A; NCBC got constitutional status as Art 338B by the 102nd Amendment (2018); the Special Officer is Art 350B; the Inter-State Council is Art 263. Note the two commissions are consecutive and easily swapped.
questions.h: 338 SC, 338A ST, 338B BC: the commissions go in the order of the letters

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Attorney General of India:
1. He must be a person qualified to be appointed as a judge of the Supreme Court.
2. He has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of both Houses of Parliament but cannot vote.
3. He has a fixed term of five years and can be removed only by impeachment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Art 76 sets the qualification and Art 88 gives speaking rights without vote. The Constitution fixes no term and prescribes no removal procedure; he holds office during the pleasure of the President.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Attorney General of India is not debarred from private legal practice.
Statement-II: The Attorney General is not a full-time government counsel and is not treated as a government servant.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Because the Attorney General is not a whole-time government counsel or government servant, he may practise privately; the limit is that he cannot advise against the Government of India or accept briefs where he is called on to advise or appear for it.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about NITI Aayog:
1. It was set up in 2015 by a resolution of the Union Cabinet and is neither a constitutional nor a statutory body.
2. The Prime Minister is its Chairperson, and the Chief Ministers of all States are members of its Governing Council.
3. Its Chief Executive Officer is appointed by the Prime Minister for a fixed tenure.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015 through a Cabinet resolution, and its Governing Council has the PM, all CMs and Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories. The CEO is appointed by the PM for a fixed tenure.

questions.q: The Planning Commission, which NITI Aayog replaced, was set up in 1950 by:
o: An Act of Parliament passed on the recommendation of the Constituent Assembly
A resolution of the Union Cabinet
questions.e: The Planning Commission was an extra-constitutional and non-statutory body created by an executive resolution of the Cabinet in March 1950. NITI Aayog also has the same executive, non-statutory character.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Non-Constitutional Bodies; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Planning)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC):
1. Following the 2019 amendment, a former judge of the Supreme Court, and not only a former Chief Justice of India, is eligible to be its Chairperson.
2. The Chairperson and members hold office for five years.
3. The Commission may not inquire into a matter if more than one year has passed since the act complained of.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019 widened eligibility to any former Supreme Court judge and cut the term from five years to three years or age 70. The one-year limit is in Section 36 of the 1993 Act, so statement 2 is the wrong one.

questions.q:
Which of the above are members of the committee that recommends the appointment of the Chairperson of the NHRC?
1. Prime Minister
2. Speaker of the Lok Sabha
3. Chief Justice of India
4. Home Minister
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The committee has the PM as head, the Speaker, the Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha, the Union Home Minister and the Leaders of Opposition in both Houses. The CJI is not on the committee; a sitting CJI is consulted for the Chairperson's appointment under the Act.

questions.q:
How many of the following are statutory (non-constitutional) bodies?
1. National Commission for Women
2. National Human Rights Commission
3. Central Vigilance Commission
4. National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
questions.e: NCW (Act of 1990), NHRC (Act of 1993) and CVC (CVC Act 2003) are statutory. NCST is constitutional under Art 338A, which is the trap.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Central Information Commission (CIC):
1. It is established under the Right to Information Act, 2005.
2. The Chief Information Commissioner is appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee headed by the Prime Minister.
3. The Chief Information Commissioner can be removed by the President only after an inquiry by the Supreme Court reports misbehaviour or incapacity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The RTI Act 2005 creates the CIC; the selection committee is the PM, the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM. Removal for misbehaviour or incapacity needs a Supreme Court report, matching the NHRC and UPSC pattern.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Central Information Commission; RTI Act 2005

questions.q: The Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) was set up in 1964 on the recommendation of:
questions.e: The K. Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption (1962-64) led to the CVC being set up by an executive resolution in 1964. It got statutory status through the CVC Act, 2003, after the Supreme Court's Vineet Narain judgment.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Central Vigilance Commission:
1. It is a multi-member body consisting of a Central Vigilance Commissioner and not more than two Vigilance Commissioners.
2. It exercises superintendence over the functioning of the Delhi Special Police Establishment insofar as it relates to the investigation of offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act.
3. It is an investigating agency that can itself conduct prosecutions in court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The CVC Act 2003 provides one Central Vigilance Commissioner and up to two Vigilance Commissioners, and gives it superintendence over the DSPE (CBI) for corruption cases. The CVC has no investigating or prosecuting machinery of its own; it advises and recommends, so statement 3 is false.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Lokpal:
1. It comprises a Chairperson and a maximum of eight members, of whom 50 per cent must be judicial members.
2. Not less than 50 per cent of its members must belong to SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities and women.
3. The Prime Minister is outside its jurisdiction in all matters.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 prescribes half judicial members and half reserved categories. The PM is covered, but not for allegations relating to international relations, external and internal security, public order, atomic energy and space, and a Lokpal full bench with a two-thirds majority must clear any inquiry.

questions.q: Who was the first Chairperson of the Lokpal of India, sworn in in March 2019?
questions.e: Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose, a former Supreme Court judge and member of the NHRC, took oath as the first Lokpal Chairperson on 23 March 2019, five years after the Act came into force.
questions.s: PIB, 23 March 2019; Laxmikanth, Lokpal and Lokayuktas

questions.q:
With reference to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), consider the following statements:
1. It derives its powers from the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946.
2. It was set up in 1963 by a resolution of the Ministry of Home Affairs.
3. The Director of the CBI is selected by a committee consisting of the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition (or the leader of the single largest opposition party) in Lok Sabha and the Chief Justice of India or a Supreme Court judge nominated by him.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The CBI is neither constitutional nor created by its own Act; its legal basis is the DSPE Act 1946, with a Home Ministry resolution of 1963. The Lokpal Act 2013 amended the DSPE Act to bring in this three-member selection committee.

questions.q: Under Article 323A of the Constitution, Parliament may by law provide for the establishment of administrative tribunals for matters relating to:
o: Recruitment and conditions of service of persons appointed to public services of the Union, States and local authorities
Levy, assessment and collection of taxes
Elections to Parliament and State Legislatures
questions.e: Art 323A covers service matters of public servants and was inserted by the 42nd Amendment (1976) on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation. Taxation, industrial disputes and elections are listed in Art 323B, and only the legislature specified there may legislate on them.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about tribunals under Articles 323A and 323B:
1. Tribunals under Article 323A can be created only by Parliament.
2. Tribunals under Article 323B can be created by Parliament and by State Legislatures on matters within their legislative competence.
3. In L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India (1997), the Supreme Court held that tribunal decisions are subject to judicial review by High Courts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Art 323A empowers only Parliament, while Art 323B allows Parliament and State Legislatures for the listed subjects. Chandra Kumar struck down the clauses excluding High Court jurisdiction, and tribunal orders can be challenged before the High Court's division bench under Arts 226 and 227.

questions.q: The National Green Tribunal (NGT) was established under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010. Which one of the following statements about it is correct?
o: It is bound by the procedure laid down in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908
Its principal bench is at Bhopal
Appeals against its orders lie to the Supreme Court
Its Chairperson must be a retired Chief Justice of a High Court
questions.e: Under Section 22 of the NGT Act, appeals lie to the Supreme Court. The NGT is guided by natural justice and is not bound by the CPC; its principal bench is in Delhi, with regional benches at Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai, and its Chairperson is a retired Supreme Court judge or a retired High Court Chief Justice.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, NGT; NGT Act 2010

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a tribunal that was merged or abolished by the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021?
o: Airports Economic Regulatory Authority Appellate Tribunal
questions.e: The Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021 abolished a number of appellate bodies, including the IPAB, the Film Certification Appellate Tribunal and the AERA Appellate Tribunal, and moved their work to High Courts or other appellate forums. The NGT was not among them.
questions.s: PRS Legislative Research, Tribunals Reforms Act 2021; Laxmikanth, Tribunals

questions.q:
Statement-I: Decisions of a tribunal created under Article 323A can be challenged before a High Court.
Statement-II: The Supreme Court in L. Chandra Kumar held that the power of judicial review of High Courts under Articles 226 and 227 is part of the basic structure of the Constitution.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
questions.e: Because judicial review by High Courts and the Supreme Court is part of the basic structure, Chandra Kumar read down the provisions barring High Court review. Tribunal decisions are therefore open to a writ challenge before the concerned High Court's division bench.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the GST Council:
1. It is a constitutional body established under Article 279A.
2. The Union Finance Minister is its Chairperson.
3. Every decision is taken by a majority of at least three-fourths of the weighted votes of members present and voting, with the Union holding one-third of the weight.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Art 279A was inserted by the 101st Amendment (2016). The Union has one-third of the weighted votes and all States together two-thirds, so the Centre can block any decision and the States cannot pass one without the Centre.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Election Commission of India:
1. The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from office in the same manner and on the same grounds as a judge of the Supreme Court.
2. Any other Election Commissioner can be removed by the President only on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner.
3. Article 324 fixes the number of Election Commissioners at two.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Proviso to Art 324(5) gives the CEC judge-like protection and the other Commissioners removal only on the CEC's recommendation. Art 324 leaves the number to the President, which is why the Commission was single-member until 1989 and multi-member since 1993.

questions.q: The appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners is presently governed by a 2023 Act. Under it, the selection committee consists of:
o: The Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha and the Chief Justice of India
The Prime Minister, the Speaker of Lok Sabha and the Union Law Minister
The Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister
The President, the Vice-President and the Prime Minister
questions.e: The 2023 Act replaced the Chief Justice of India with a Union Cabinet Minister, which departed from the Supreme Court's interim direction in Anoop Baranwal (2023) that the CJI sit on the committee.
questions.s: CEC and Other ECs (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023

questions.q:
With reference to the State Public Service Commissions, consider the following statements:
1. The Chairman and members are appointed by the Governor.
2. They can be removed from office by the Governor on grounds of misbehaviour.
3. Parliament can set up a Joint State Public Service Commission for two or more States if the Legislatures of the States concerned pass resolutions to that effect.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Art 316 gives appointment by the Governor, but removal is by the President after a Supreme Court inquiry (Art 317). Joint Commissions under Art 315(2) are created by Parliament on requests from the States' legislatures.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the State Human Rights Commission (SHRC):
1. Its Chairperson is appointed by the Governor on the recommendation of a committee headed by the Chief Minister.
2. It can inquire into violations of human rights relating to matters in the State List and the Concurrent List.
3. Its Chairperson can be removed by the Governor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 provides for a Governor's appointment on a committee headed by the CM, and for inquiry into State and Concurrent List matters. Removal is by the President after a Supreme Court inquiry, so statement 3 fails.

questions.q: Which one of the following is correct about the National Commission for Minorities?
o: It was set up under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992 and Jains were notified as a minority community in 2014
It is a constitutional body under Article 338B
Parsis were notified as a minority community in 2014
Buddhists and Sikhs were not notified as minority communities at the national level
questions.e: The NCM is statutory. The Centre notified Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists and Zoroastrians (Parsis) in 1993 and added Jains in 2014; Art 338B is the NCBC.

questions.q: The 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2018 is associated with which of the following?
o: Granting constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes
Establishing the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
Setting up the National Commission for Women as a constitutional body
questions.e: The 102nd Amendment inserted Art 338B (NCBC) and Arts 342A and 366(26C). The GST Council came with the 101st Amendment and the NCST with the 89th.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, National Commission for Backward Classes

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Advocate General of a State:
1. He is appointed by the Governor.
2. He must be qualified for appointment as a High Court judge.
3. He holds office for a fixed term of five years.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Art 165 provides appointment by the Governor and the same qualification as a High Court judge. His tenure is not fixed and he holds office during the Governor's pleasure.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Advocate General of the State

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT):
1. It was set up under the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985, which was passed under Article 323A.
2. Its jurisdiction extends to members of the armed forces of the Union.
3. Its decisions can be challenged before the High Court under Articles 226 and 227.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 1985 Act implemented Art 323A and the CAT began functioning in 1985. The Act excludes members of the armed forces, officers and staff of the Supreme Court and High Courts and the secretarial staff of Parliament; after Chandra Kumar the High Court can review CAT orders.

questions.q: Which one of the following articles of the Constitution deals with the adjudication of inter-State river water disputes?
questions.e: Art 262 lets Parliament provide for adjudication of such disputes and bar the courts, including the Supreme Court, from deciding them; the Inter-State Water Disputes Act, 1956 did so. Art 263 is the Inter-State Council and Art 131 is the Supreme Court's original jurisdiction.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Inter-State Council and the Zonal Councils:
1. The Inter-State Council is established by the President under Article 263.
2. Zonal Councils were created by the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
3. The Union Home Minister is the Chairman of each Zonal Council.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Inter-State Council was set up in 1990 on the Sarkaria Commission's advice, and the five Zonal Councils are statutory bodies under the 1956 Act chaired by the Union Home Minister. Art 263 only enables the President to set up such a Council, so it is created by a Presidential order and not by the Constitution itself.

questions.q: The Solicitor General of India:
o: Is appointed under Article 76 and has a fixed term
Is a constitutional officer with the right to speak in Parliament
Is elected by the Bar Council of India
Is not mentioned in the Constitution and assists the Attorney General
questions.e: Art 76 provides only for the Attorney General. The Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General are law officers assisting him but have no constitutional status.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Central Information Commission:
1. The President may remove the Chief Information Commissioner if he is adjudged an insolvent.
2. The President may remove him if he engages during his term of office in any paid employment outside the duties of his office.
3. In either of these cases the President must first obtain the Supreme Court's report.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Under Section 14 of the RTI Act, insolvency, conviction for an offence involving moral turpitude, paid outside employment or unfitness by infirmity are grounds for removal without any Supreme Court reference. A Supreme Court inquiry is required only for proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
questions.s: RTI Act 2005, Sec 14; Laxmikanth, Central Information Commission

questions.q: The 14th Finance Commission raised the share of States in the divisible pool of Union taxes from 32 per cent to:
questions.e: The 14th Finance Commission, chaired by Y. V. Reddy, recommended 42 per cent for 2015-20, a large step towards fiscal federalism. The 15th Finance Commission set the share at 41 per cent for 2021-26 after adjusting for the creation of the Union Territory of Ladakh.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Central Vigilance Commission:
1. The Central Vigilance Commissioner holds office for four years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
2. The Commissioner is appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee comprising the Prime Minister, the Union Home Minister and the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha.
3. The Commission submits its annual report to the Parliament directly.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The CVC Act 2003 sets a term of four years or age 65, and the Home Minister sits on the selection committee. The report goes to the President, who lays it before each House of Parliament, so the CVC does not submit it to Parliament directly.

questions.q: In which of the following judgments did the Supreme Court strike down Section 6A of the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946, which required prior Government approval to investigate senior officers?
o: Vineet Narain v. Union of India
S. R. Bommai v. Union of India
Prakash Singh v. Union of India
questions.e: In Subramanian Swamy (2014) the Court held Section 6A violated Art 14 as it protected corrupt officers by rank. Vineet Narain (1997) had given earlier directions for the CBI's independence and the CVC.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Central Bureau of Investigation; Subramanian Swamy (2014)

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Lokpal cannot inquire into a complaint relating to an offence committed more than seven years before the complaint is made.
Statement-II: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 prescribes a time limit to prevent stale allegations from being inquired into.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
questions.e: The Act bars complaints about offences more than seven years old, so the limit is the Act's own safeguard.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Lokpal and Lokayuktas; Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013

questions.q: Which one of the following bodies was established with its status derived directly from a Cabinet or executive resolution and not from any Act or the Constitution?
questions.e: NITI Aayog is created by a Cabinet resolution. The CCI (Competition Act 2002), NCW (1990 Act) and CIC (RTI Act 2005) are all statutory.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Finance Commission:
1. The Chairman must be a person with experience in public affairs.
2. The four other members must include one with specialised knowledge of economics.
3. A person who is a High Court judge, or qualified to be one, may be appointed as a member.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951, made under Art 280, lays down these qualifications: a member may be a judge or one qualified as a judge, or have special knowledge of finance and accounts, administrative experience, or economics. The Chairman is chosen from persons with public affairs experience.

questions.q:
The Comptroller and Auditor General of India audits which of the following?
1. Receipts and expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India
2. Accounts of the Contingency Fund and the Public Account of India
3. Accounts of a government company, when appointed as its auditor in the manner under the Companies Act, 2013
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Art 149 and the CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 cover all three Funds of the Union and of the States. For companies, the CAG appoints the auditors of a Government company and supplements their audit.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Comptroller and Auditor General of India

questions.q: Which one of the following is a constitutional body?
questions.e: The Finance Commission is under Art 280. NHRC (1993 Act), CVC (2003 Act) and Lokpal (2013 Act) are statutory bodies.

questions.q: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST) is provided for under which Article?
questions.e: Art 338A, inserted by the 89th Amendment Act, 2003, creates the NCST. Art 339 deals with control of the Union over administration of Scheduled Areas and welfare of Scheduled Tribes.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about tribunals after the Supreme Court's judgment in L. Chandra Kumar:
1. Tribunals can adjudicate the constitutional validity of the parent statute under which they are constituted.
2. Tribunals continue to act as courts of first instance for the areas they are empowered to cover.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Chandra Kumar held that tribunals may test the validity of subordinate legislation and of statutes other than their own parent statute, so statement 1 is wrong. They do act as courts of first instance in their areas, with appeal to the High Court's division bench.

questions.q: Which of the following bodies has the power under the Constitution to make recommendations on the principles governing grants-in-aid to the States out of the Consolidated Fund of India?
questions.e: Art 280(3)(b) lets the Finance Commission recommend the principles for grants-in-aid under Art 275. NITI Aayog has no constitutional role in this.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Finance Commission : Article 280
2. Joint Public Service Commission for two or more States : Article 315
3. Attorney General of India : Article 78
4. Election Commission : Article 324
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 4 are correct (Art 315(2) provides for a joint commission). The Attorney General is under Art 76; Art 78 lists the duties of the Prime Minister to furnish information to the President.
